items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing a fetal
infant mortality review board
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6044

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing a
fetal infant mortality review board

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA:

The purpose of this bill is to create a statewide fetal infant mortality
review board that would investigate fetal, neonatal, and post-neonatal
deaths across the state; identify the root causes of these horrific
outcomes; and issue recommendations for best practices in avoiding these
outcomes.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill establishes both the review board and its compo-
sition. The board would be tasked with assessing the causes of fetal and
infant deaths, determining the factors which lead to these deaths, and
disseminating strategies for reducing the risk of these deaths. In addi-
tion to assessing health-related factors, the board is to consider
racial and economic disparities affecting these outcomes.  The board
would be allowed to review pertinent records - as well as any statements
made by relevant individuals on a voluntary basis - provided that such
records and statements are redacted prior to being transmitted to the
review board. Records, statements, and other information shall be
redacted to protect the personal identifying information of the fetus or
infant, the parents of the fetus or infant, and the medical profes-
sionals involved (including the relevant hospital or facility). All
records received and internal documents not meant for public consumption
shall not be made open or available to the public. Such information
shall not be discoverable or admissible as evidence in any action in any
court or before any other tribunal, board, agency, or person. Section
two of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Fetal and infant deaths during the perinatal period have a detrimental
impact on the person giving birth, their family, and the community at
large. This bill would establish a statewide Fetal Infant Mortality
Review Board (FIMR) to identity the root causes of these horrific
outcomes and recommend action-oriented solutions.

Many states, as well as Washington DC and the commonwealth of Puerto
Rico, have implemented such boards to help address this urgent issue.
These boards interview parents, review pertinent records and reports,
and subsequently recommend interventions that can reduce the risk of
fetal and infant deaths. A statewide FIMR would bring new insights,
helping us lower the fetal and infant mortality rate, especially in
communities whose rates far exceed the state average. The infant mortal-
ity rate in New York State is relatively low when compared to other
states. However, the state's overall success in this area is not shared
equally across our communities. Low-income communities and communities
of color have infant mortality rates that are two or even three times
higher than the statewide average. An in-depth review of individual and
aggregate fetal/infant deaths and morbidity cases would shed light on
the root causes of poor pregnancy outcomes, and hopefully improve them.
 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATION FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

TBD.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law and the administrative code of the city
of New York, in relation to establishing fetal and infant mortality review
boards
B.lawCode: Add §2509-b, Pub Health L; add §17-166.1, NYC Ad Cd
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6044B

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law and the administrative code of the
city of New York, in relation to establishing fetal and infant mortality
review boards

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to create a statewide fetal infant mortality
review board that would investigate fetal, neonatal, and post-neonatal
deaths across the state; identify the root causes of these horrific
outcomes; and issue recommendations for best practices in avoiding these
outcomes.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: The public health law is amended by adding a new section

§ 2509-b:

(a) Defines "Board"; expands the definition to include "state board" or
a board operating in New York City with or without an agreement with the
Commissioner of Health defined as "city board".

(b) Defines "Fetal and infant death".

(c) Defines "Severe fetal and infant morbidity".

(d) Defines "City commissioner".

Section 2:

(a) Establishes within the New York City department of health and mental
hygiene a review board for the purpose of reviewing fetal and infant
deaths. Provides guidelines for what \ the board will review, findings
to disseminate, and make recommendations that contribute to the
prevention of fetal and infant mortality and morbidity.

(b) Provides discretion to the commissioner of the department of health
to enter into an agreement with the city of New York, through the
department of health and mental hygiene.

(c) Provides autonomy to the city of New York to establish its own fetal
and infant mortality board through it's department of health and mental
hygiene despite whether there is an agreement with the commissioner of
the State department of health.

Section 3:

(a) Provides the composition of the review board.

(b) Provides number of appointments from each legislative house, and the
Governor.

(c) Provides the term length of each appointed member, and discretion to
the commissioner to reappoint state board members to 3 additional years.
(d) Provides quorum requirements.

(e) Provides board member attendance requirements.

(f) Provides minimum meeting requirements.

(g) Provides indemnification requirements.

(h) Provides members of the state board will not be compensated but will
be reimbursed for their ordinary and necessary expenses of partic-
ipation.

(i) Provides that membership on a board shall not disqualify any person
from holding any public office or employment.

Section 4:

(a) Provides discretionary authority to the commissioner to request
information, and which entities shall comply with providing information.

(b) Provides authority to the commissioner for the solicitation and
reception of voluntary information that is oral and written, and for the
transcription of oral statements in any case before the board.

(c) Requires redaction of any personal information prior to transmittal
of any information.

(d) Prevents information received or transmitted inadmissible in any
civil proceeding.

Section 5: Required actions to be taken by each board.

Section 6: Maintenance of confidentiality regarding personal informa-
tion. Prevents admissibility of such information as evidence in any
action in any court.

Section 7: The commissioner and the city commissioner may use findings
and recommendations of the boards to develop best practices and actions
for health care providers to implement.

§ 2. The administrative code of the city of New York is amended by
adding a new section 17166.1. This new section includes all of the same
provisions that amend the public health law by adding section

§ 2509-b.

§ 3. This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a
law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Fetal and infant deaths during the perinatal period have a detrimental
impact on the person giving birth, their family, and the community at
large. This bill would establish a statewide Fetal Infant Mortality
Review Board (FIMR) to identify the root causes of these horrific
outcomes and recommend action-oriented solutions. Many states, as well
as Washington DC and the commonwealth of Puerto Rico, have implemented
such boards to help address this urgent issue. These boards interview
parents, review pertinent records and reports, and subsequently recom-
mend interventions that can reduce the risk of fetal and infant deaths.
A statewide FIMR would bring new insights, helping us lower the fetal
and infant mortality rate, especially in 2/3 communities whose rates far
exceed the state average. The infant mortality rate in New York State is
relatively low when compared to other states. However, the state's over-
all success in this area is not shared equally across our communities.
Low-income communities and communities of color have infant mortality
rates that are two or even three times higher than the statewide aver-
age. An in-depth review of individual and aggregate fetal/infant deaths
and morbidity cases would shed light on the root causes
 of poor pregnancy outcomes, and hopefully improve them.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Establishes fetal and infant mortality review boards to study fetal and infant mortality and morbidity and make recommendations on policies, best practices, and strategies to reduce fetal and infant mortality and morbidity.
